transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-21
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Lina Martinez (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (BlueCascade Head of ML), Sara Huang (Infra), Chris O'Neill (Product)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect): Discussed embeddings scale, vector DB choice, hybrid reranking, throughput needs (~300-1k QPS), dataset size ~120M vectors, regulatory constraints (EU). Next steps captured.

[00:00:00] Lina: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lina, AE at Redwood. Quick intros?
[00:00:08] Mark: Yeah hi, Mark Rivera, I run the ML team at BlueCascade. We've got Sara and Chris with me.
[00:00:12] Sara: Sara Huang, infra eng, I'll be the point on deployment and network stuff.
[00:00:16] Chris: Chris O'Neill, product, focused on latency and UX.
[00:00:20] Raj: Raj Patel, Redwood SE, I'll dig into performance and indexing.
[00:00:26] Lina: Great. High level, you sent over a note that you're evaluating embeddings + rerank for a semantic search product and you want options across hosted, dedicated, and private. Is that a fair summary?
[00:00:36] Mark: Yes. We're especially worried about scale — we expect around 120 million document vectors, each vector currently 768 dims but might move to 1536 for higher quality.
[00:00:46] Chris: And product wants tail latency under 120ms for interactive search, with a background higher-throughput batch use case.
[00:00:53] Sara: Also need EU data residency and we need KMS integration for keys.
[00:00:58] Lina: Perfect. Raj, want to take us through how Redwood typically handles this set of constraints?
[00:01:04] Raj: Sure. So there are a few axes: embedding size, index strategy (HNSW, IVF, PQ/quantization), and whether you do hybrid search — e.g., BM25 or lexical first-pass plus dense rerank. For 120M vectors, Faiss/IVF+PQ or Milvus with vector compression are common. Hosted can work but at large scale dedicated pools or private are more cost predictable.
[00:01:28] Mark: We're leaning away from fully managed vector DB vendors because we want tight control over data and cost, but using a VDB is likely. Does Redwood integrate directly with Milvus/Pinecone or do you expect customers to run the index separately?
[00:01:41] Raj: We integrate flexibly. For hosted customers we often pair Redwood-generated embeddings with Pinecone or our managed annotation for small workloads. For dedicated/private, teams commonly run Milvus or FAISS in their VPC and we route embedding generation + rerank inference to Redwood Dedicated nodes, so the flow is: document indexing job produces vectors -> stored in customer's selected DB -> query flow calls DB for top-K -> Redwood does rerank on top results with cross-encoder.
[00:02:04] Sara: How do you handle throughput? Our target is 300 QPS sustained for search, spiking to 1k QPS. Rerank is heavier — doing cross-encoder on top 50 hits would be expensive.
[00:02:15] Raj: Right. Typical pattern is lexical filter to reduce candidates to ~100, then lightweight dense dot-product to get top 50, then cross-encoder rerank on top 10-20. On Redwood Dedicated, you configure batching, max latency SLOs, and we can do GPU batching for the cross-encoder to amortize cost. For your numbers, we would recommend a dedicated fleet with autoscale and burst capacity.
[00:02:40] Chris: What's the cost ballpark to do cross-encoder rerank at that QPS? We have a tight budget.
[00:02:45] Lina: We'll send a detailed pricing model. Very rough: per-token compute for cross-encoder plus embedding generation. For rerank you can reduce tokenization cost by using truncated contexts; also quantization and smaller rerank models can lower cost. We'll include a few options (full cross-encoder vs distilled).
[00:02:59] Mark: We also care about embedding dimensionality. If we reduce dims from 1536 to 768 we save storage and maybe speed, but quality loss unknown. Have you seen real diffs?
[00:03:09] Raj: It depends on task. For semantic matching, 768 often hits diminishing returns vs 1536 for subtle distinctions. But you can use product-specific eval sets — Redwood's Optimize tool can run A/B on embedding dimensionality and report precision@k/regression. We can run a quick eval on your sample.
[00:03:27] Sara: The storage side — 120M * 1536 dims floats is huge. We're planning to store compressed vectors using PQ; what's Redwood's guidance on index config?
[00:03:37] Raj: For that scale, IVF-PQ with 8-16 bytes/code and a moderate number of centroids is common. Use HNSW for memory-perf tradeoff on read-heavy workloads but HNSW memory scales with dataset size. Milvus + GPU indexing can help build indexes faster. Also consider quantized embeddings (int8/4-bit) from embedding model to cut storage. We'll put together recommended configs.
[00:04:00] Mark: Regarding private deployment — we need the control plane on our side, and logs kept in our region. Is Redwood Private a self-hosted control plane or do you need outbound to Redwood?
[00:04:10] Lina: Redwood Private gives you a customer-managed control plane option; you can run the control plane in your cloud region, with optional offline/on-prem packages for air-gapped. Our telemetry hooks are configurable — you can route logs to your SIEM. We support KMS/HSM integrations.
[00:04:25] Sara: Ok. And SSO/SAML and RBAC?
[00:04:28] Raj: Full SSO/SAML and fine-grained RBAC, audit logs per token, and per-route tracing in the console. We'll share SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
[00:04:40] Chris: A couple of technical clarifications: KV cache — you mentioned prefix caching. How effective is that for search rerank?
[00:04:48] Raj: KV cache helps when queries share context or you do conversational flows. For one-off search queries it helps less. But we have prefix caching for embeddings too — frequently accessed doc vectors can be cached at the serving layer to shave tens of ms. Combined with batching, it can improve throughput significantly.
[00:05:05] Mark: About vector DB vendors — you said Redwood can integrate with Pinecone and Milvus. Any customers running Weaviate?
[00:05:12] Raj: Yeah, some customers use Weaviate for schema/metadata-first flows. We do connector integrations; if there's a bespoke store our APIs are flexible.
[00:05:20] Sara: For benchmarking, what would you need from us?
[00:05:23] Raj: A representative 10M sample, the embedding model you're using or willing to try, and a set of query prompts and relevance labels if you have them. We'll run tok/latency/throughput with different batch sizes and GPU instance types.
[00:05:36] Mark: We can provide a 10M subset and a small set of labeled queries (~500).
[00:05:40] Lina: Great. We'll also include a few config permutations: dims 768 vs 1536, PQ8 vs PQ16, and using a distilled cross-encoder.
[00:05:50] Chris: How do you recommend doing fallbacks? If Dedicated capacity is saturated do you fall back to hosted smaller models?
[00:05:57] Raj: Exactly. Smart routing can failover to a lighter model or to a Redwood hosted regional pool. You can set per-customer policies: latency-first vs cost-first.
[00:06:07] Mark: Any gotchas with OpenSearch hybrid capabilities? We're considering keeping lexical in OpenSearch and dense in a separate vector DB.
[00:06:15] Raj: That's a common architecture. Best practice is to do lexical first-pass in OpenSearch then call the vector DB and rerank. Be careful about duplication of metadata and keeping consistent doc IDs. We often recommend adding a lightweight join-store or sync pipeline.
[00:06:30] Sara: Network topology — we want everything in EU region, and private endpoints. Can Redwood Dedicated be VPC peered?
[00:06:36] Lina: Yes, Dedicated pools can be set up in specific regions and peered via VPC peering/private link depending on cloud. Private deployment is fully inside your VPC.
[00:06:44] Chris: Security question: does Redwood persist raw documents when doing rerank?
[00:06:48] Raj: For inference we only persist what you configure. We can disable retention for hosted API or route everything through your private deployment so no raw docs leave your environment. We'll document defaults.
[00:06:59] Mark: Back to performance — can you give a rough microbenchmark: cross-encoder on A100 vs T4 for batch size 16 on 128 token inputs?
[00:07:08] Raj: Very rough numbers: on A100 you'd see sub-20ms per example with good batching, T4 more like 35-60ms depending on batch efficiency. Those numbers are noisy and depend on model size and whether you use int8 quant. We'll run your specific tests.
[00:07:22] Chris: If we need to reduce cost significantly, what are the biggest levers?
[00:07:26] Raj: Short list: reduce embedding dim, use PQ/quantization, reduce cross-encoder size (distil or two-stage), increase first-pass recall to lower rerank load, and use caching for frequent queries. Also Dedicated reserved capacity pricing helps.
[00:07:41] Mark: For our timeline — we'd like a POC in the next 6-8 weeks to validate latency and cost. Is that reasonable?
[00:07:47] Lina: Yes. Typical POC path: discovery (this call), benchmark run with sample data, then 2-week test on dedicated/dev cluster, then expand. We'll draft a POC plan.
[00:07:56] Sara: On logs and auditing, we need per-request logs forwarded to our SIEM with masked PII. Is that supported?
[00:08:02] Raj: You can configure log forwarding and masking policies. We'll include guidance in the security pack.
[00:08:09] Chris: Any regulatory red flags with EU residency and KMS?
[00:08:13] Lina: Not typically — we can host in EU regions and support KMS in your tenant. For some industries you'll need private deployment. We'll share patterns.
[00:08:22] Mark: Ok let's talk about concrete next steps and owners.
[00:08:26] Lina: I'll capture action items. Raj will run benchmarks once we have the sample. We'll send security docs. Let's confirm dates: can you ship sample by March 28?
[00:08:36] Mark: Yes we can aim for that.
[00:08:39] Sara: We'll get it to you, with some query labels.
[00:08:42] Lina: Great. Any other questions?
[00:08:45] Chris: One small question — does Redwood offer an embedding store so we don't run a separate vector DB?
[00:08:50] Raj: For smaller scale we have a managed embeddings index, but at 120M we typically recommend customer-managed DB for cost and control. The managed option is convenient for prototyping.
[00:08:59] Mark: Makes sense.
[00:09:02] Lina: Ok recap: Redwood to run benchmark on a 10M sample with multiple configs; share security pack; propose POC plan and pricing. We'll schedule a technical deep dive on indexing (Milvus/FAISS choices) week of April 7.
[00:09:17] Mark: Sounds good, thanks.
[00:09:19] Lina: Thanks all.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-hear — e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cash" in earlier runs; proper names may be slightly off.
